fredericksburg-baptist-church.assessment: Fredericksburg Baptist Church is one of the older Baptist congregations in the city, located on historic Princess Anne Street. The mission language is straightforwardly Christ-centered — 'on mission together, striving to continue the work of Christ' with commitments to 'the praise of God and the proclamation of the word of God' and 'the preservation, instruction, and spreading of the Gospel.' That's a healthy public-facing posture. The honest concern is BGAV affiliation: the Baptist General Association of Virginia is the moderate Virginia Baptist stream, separate from SBC, and the denominational structure allows women in pastoral roles and leans progressive on several fronts. Pastor David Haun's theological convictions are unknown. Before visiting, Moop should confirm the church's stance on Scripture inerrancy, women in ministry, and elder accountability. The Princess Anne address is prime downtown Fredericksburg — a historic congregation worth investigating. (Also operates as "FXBG Baptist Church" with shorter URL/branding via fxbgbaptist.org.)

fredericksburg-church-of-christ.assessment: Fredericksburg Church of Christ has a lot going for it: high Scripture authority, Trinitarian orthodoxy, complementarian leadership with male elder plurality, expository DNA, and no cultural drift indicators. The congregation explicitly states they are 'not a denomination, but simply Christians that belong to the body of believers of which Christ is the head' — that's a healthy posture. The hard stop for a faith-alone evangelical like Moop: Churches of Christ traditionally teach that baptism is necessary for salvation, not merely a sign of it. This is the theological fault line that separates the Restoration Movement from mainstream evangelicalism — and it's a real one. Not a cult, not heresy in the broad sense, but incompatible with sola fide. Worth a conversation with leadership to clarify their exact position on baptism and salvation before getting deeper. Some congregations in this tradition have moved toward a more grace-emphasis soteriology; some have not.

fredericksburg-presbyterian-church-pcusa.assessment: Fredericksburg Presbyterian Church on Princess Anne Street is a historic congregation with over 200 years of ministry in the city — that heritage is real and worth noting. However, it affiliates with the Presbyterian Church (USA), which formally departed from biblical authority in 2015 by voting to approve same-sex marriage, ordains women at all levels of church government, and does not affirm biblical inerrancy. The church's website language about 'preserving God's creation' and 'honoring gifts' suggests alignment with the denomination's progressive trajectory. For a man committed to complementarian Christianity, biblical inerrancy, and historic sexual ethics, PCUSA is a disqualifying affiliation. This entry serves as a reference so men visiting downtown Fredericksburg understand why this historic church, despite its beautiful building and heritage, is not the right choice theologically.

The congregation may have sincere Christ-loving people in the pews, but the institutional framework is compromised.
